extracted.intended_audience: owners and operators of CCR surface impoundments, facility operators, state and federal regulators, environmental consultants, and environmental attorneys participating in CCR rule implementation and notice-and-comment
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretive and implementation guidance for determining when a CCR surface impoundment is a "legacy CCR surface impoundment" (i.e., whether it "contained both CCR and liquids" on or after October 19, 2015), how to determine presence of liquids/free liquids, what documentation is required, and what requirements apply for closed or dewatered units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legacy CCR Surface Impoundment — contains both CCR and liquids on or after October 19, 2015
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered a "legacy CCR surface impoundment" a CCR surface impoundment must have contained both CCR and liquids on or after October 19, 2015; the final rule further defines what it means to contain both CCR and liquid by reference to §257.102(d)(2)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Units must be evaluated as of October 19, 2015. Units that do not contain both CCR and liquid on or after that date are not legacy impoundments under this rule. See Unit III.B.2.b.i and §257.102(d)(2)(i) for further explanation. An impoundment that still contains liquids on or after that date is considered an inactive impoundment and will be regulated as a legacy impoundment when located at an inactive facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'liquids' — inclusive list
rubrics_metrics.description: The term "liquids" includes free water, porewater, standing water, and groundwater, regardless of their source (e.g., precipitation, sluice water, surface water infiltration, or groundwater intrusion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA adopts the ordinary dictionary meaning and incorporates it into §257.53. The source of the liquid does not change its designation or its potential to create leachate or contribute to hydraulic head; all such liquids are relevant to risk and regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'contains' — presence of liquid in unit
rubrics_metrics.description: An impoundment "contains" liquid if there is liquid in the impoundment; that is, it has water within it, even if water continues to leak from the unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if surface water has been decanted, a surface impoundment where CCR remains saturated (or otherwise contains liquid) will be considered to "contain" liquids. Ordinary meaning governs: if liquids are present in the unit it contains liquids unless the facility can demonstrate free liquids have been eliminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dewatered determination based on §257.102(d)(2)(i)
rubrics_metrics.description: A unit is considered dewatered if it met the performance standard in §257.102(d)(2)(i): "Free liquids must be eliminated by removing liquid wastes or solidifying the remaining wastes and waste residues."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires elimination of both standing liquid and readily separable porewater in any sediment at the base of the impoundment. If a facility can document free liquids were permanently eliminated prior to October 19, 2015, the unit will not be treated as a legacy impoundment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free liquids — regulatory definition and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Free liquids are defined at §257.53 to mean "liquids that readily separate from the solid portion of a waste under ambient temperature and pressure."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This encompasses standing liquids and readily separable porewater. Residual bound porewater that will not readily drain under ambient conditions is not treated as free liquids and is less likely to be the focus of regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulate based on presence of free liquids (risk-focused threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA focuses on the presence of free liquids because these drive risk (creation of leachate, contribution to hydraulic head and flow). The operator is not required to remove all moisture, only free liquids required under §257.102(d)(2)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA intends to regulate units where free liquids remain (substantial hydraulic head/leachate risk). Periodic rainfall that does not produce free liquids (e.g., readily absorbed) would not trigger regulation; units with free liquids remain subject to requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation expectation and "good faith" effort to determine legacy status
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA expects owners and operators of inactive impoundments at inactive facilities to develop a strategy to gather readily available and reliable information to determine whether the unit meets the definition of a legacy CCR surface impoundment; EPA does not require records that no longer exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, after making a good faith effort, a facility is genuinely unable to obtain information to document that the impoundment contained both CCR and liquids on October 19, 2015, the unit would not be regulated as a legacy impoundment. EPA will not require impossible-to-obtain historical records (e.g., lost documents, unavailable employees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable methods and tools to identify or demonstrate elimination of free liquids
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools currently used include soil borings, cone penetrometers, installation of piezometers, monitoring wells, vibrating wire piezometers, and analogous geotechnical/hydraulic characterization tools; EPA has developed a memorandum describing methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA indicates these methods are commonly used by industry to investigate and close surface impoundments. The memorandum in the docket summarizes current methods and tools available to determine whether free liquids have been eliminated; the agency will accept appropriate technical demonstrations (e.g., piezometer data, stratigraphy mapping).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of units closed with waste in place prior to effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: A facility that completed closure with waste in place before the effective date of this final rule would be subject only to the closure performance standards in §257.102(d), and the post-closure care requirements (i.e., groundwater monitoring and corrective action, if necessary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If closure was completed under a regulatory authority's oversight (e.g., pursuant to a Federal or State cleanup order) the facility could be subject to even fewer requirements; EPA is deferring site-specific adequacy determinations to subsequent permitting authorities in the interim, subjecting these units only to a post-closure care permit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure-by-removal (§257.102(c)) as a basis for lack of further federal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA agrees it lacks jurisdiction over a site where the owner/operator can document that it meets the standard for closure by removal in §257.102(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities that can document meeting §257.102(c) will not be subject to further requirements under this rule; the final rule retains the provision specifying that any facility that documents that this standard has been met will not be subject to any further requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal jurisdiction depends on presence of disposed solid waste, not only CCR presence
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's jurisdiction rests on the presence of solid waste that 'is disposed of' at the site, not solely the presence of CCR; residual CCR leachate or CCR constituents remaining in soil or aquifer maintain the presence of solid waste and EPA retains jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal of CCR does not necessarily demonstrate EPA lacks jurisdiction unless the closure-by-removal standard is documented as met. Presence of residual contamination can keep the site within federal authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units at inactive facilities considered legacy even if closed under State law or in process of closing
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the final rule, an impoundment that still contains liquids on or after October 19, 2015 is considered an inactive impoundment under §257.53 and a legacy CCR surface impoundment when located at an inactive facility, even if it is considered "closed" under State law or is in the process of closing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State closure status does not by itself remove the unit from federal regulation if free liquids remain. Conversely, units fully dewatered prior to October 19, 2015 and documented as such would not be legacy impoundments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that presence of free liquids be verifiable and measurable
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA clarifies it is concerned with presence of readily separable porewater (free liquids) which can be verified by technical equipment such as piezometers and other field methods, and has provided a memorandum describing methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This resolves concerns about measurement difficulty for porewater; EPA expects technical demonstrations (piezometer readings, soil borings, cone penetrometer data, etc.). The agency also indicates what tests and sampling approaches may be appropriate (and that these are documented in the docket memorandum).

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold/amount concerns — not 'any amount' of moisture triggers regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA rejects the notion that a unit containing any amount of water (e.g., transient ponding from rainfall) should automatically be regulated; the focus is on free liquids that readily separate and pose risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic rainfall that is readily absorbed and does not produce free liquids will not result in regulation as a legacy impoundment. Conversely, units that accumulate substantial volumes (e.g., due to regional rainfall without effective cover) may contain free liquids and meet the definition.
